title: The 8 Levels of Train Phone Privacy
house: Fruitopolis, a bustling metropolis where produce people commute daily on the 7:15 Express train, guarding their phone screens like state secrets.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never blinks.
links: The bitter lemon in Level 2 mentions a generous commuter who always tips the station barista.
The quiet pear in Level 5 drops a glowing gold coin near the ticket gates that the avocado finds.
The dragon fruit from Level 7 leaves behind an empty espresso cup on the exact seat the orange sits on in Level 4.

levels.open_loop: What hidden app on the passenger's screen made the giant coconut gasp and grab the phone?

gegenspieler.tat: Snatches the phone away and reads the private chat out loud to the entire carriage, pointing mockingly at the 12% on his forehead and laughing hysterically at his misery.

levels.name: Pip, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on the train. Level 1. 2,000 euros in debt and my boss is reading live in the open-plan office while I cry in the stinking toilet. I am Pip, a pathetic strawberry person with a drooping green stem hat, clutching my shattered phone on the 7:15 morning express train while my hands shake violently. Who texts their strict boss at 6 AM about sobbing in the supply closet like a hopeless loser? I desperately slam my cracked phone screen-first against my heaving chest, my strawberry seeds turning ghostly pale from pure, unadulterated terror. That is when the giant coconut towering above me leaned down, snatched the device right out of my sweating grip, and shouted my deepest shame to every single commuter on the carriage. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Cleo, 29, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on the train. Level 2. Only 410 dollars in my bank account and I am desperately hiding my pathetic balance from the ruthless financial advisor sitting right next to me. I am Cleo, a bright orange person with peel-texture skin and a stained barista apron, riding the early commuter train after suffering through a grueling double shift. Is that all you make after working eighty hours like a peasant? The lemon monster snarls, grabbing my phone out of my hands and reading my exact bank balance out loud while mocking my miserable life. He points directly at the 410 dollars glowing on my forehead and starts laughing hysterically, humiliating me in front of everyone. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Kai, 34, Botanist
levels.story: The 8 levels of hiding your screen on the train. Level 3. 1,850 dollars a month and I am frantically swiping left on a dating app so my boss doesn't see my secret profile. I'm Kai, a vibrant green broccoli person with a bushy florets head, sweating bullets in the crowded aisle of the metro. Looking for love on public Wi-Fi? How pathetic. I jam my elbow against my ribs, pressing the phone screen so hard against my jacket that the OLED panel distorts. An incoming video call pops up, and she leaned down to utter those exact words. You'll see that in Level 4.
